text.p: Spanish government bonds ended sharply higher on Friday, with the 10-year bono yield under seven percent amid gains in other European bonds, dealers said.
Further progress would hinge on foreign markets, although in principle traders were loathe to specify resistance levels.
"This could go up and up. There's no reference levels and the market just doesn't seem to get tired, particularly the Bund," said Jose Ramon Nunez, a bond analyst at Benito y Monjardin brokerage.
EMU euphoria is still the key factor behind the drive, dealers said.
"The market simply devours all the paper it comes across," said another analyst.
The spread versus Bunds was steady at 136 basis points after the German bond added nearly a full percentage point.
All eyes will now be on Tuesday's Bank of Spain regular repurchase auction, with some expecting a key rate cut in the short-term from the current 6.75 percent rate.
